summary:
Mammillaria theresae is a small, rare cactus clinging to life in the high mountain passes of Durango, Mexico, at elevations between 2,150 and 2,300 meters. Known from perhaps only two sites a few kilometers apart, it has spent its existence in quiet isolation among rocky slopes, its entire world contained within a stretch of land that may span as little as 25 square kilometers.

What has brought this species to the edge is not nature, but human desire. Illegal collectors have targeted it relentlessly, drawn by its rarity — the very quality that makes it so vulnerable. Road construction has further carved into its already diminished habitat. Today, its population continues to shrink, and the silence where it once grew tells its own somber story.
